discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting artificial atoms to microwave photons
motivation: The 2025 Prize recognized that Josephson circuits behave as macroscopic quantum objects. The next decisive step was learning to couple and control them with light. In 2004 Blais and co-workers proposed, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated, strong coupling between a single superconducting qubit and a single microwave photon in an on-chip resonator. This circuit QED realized cavity quantum electrodynamics in a new regime, with coupling strengths far beyond those reachable with atoms. It led to dispersive quantum non-demolition readout, photon-number-resolved spectroscopy, resonator-mediated two-qubit gates, the Purcell-protected transmon and bosonic encodings. Today it is the architecture behind essentially every superconducting quantum processor, including recent below-threshold demonstrations of surface-code error correction. The work opened a new field of microwave quantum optics and turned fragile circuits into measurable, scalable quantum hardware.
